name: Pale flesh
lede: Pale flesh is a soft, warm tan that goes back to Werner's early-nineteenth-century color system, and it shares its exact screen color with a second library name, Flesh Red.

sections.title: A tan from an old naturalist's chart
sections.body:
The library traces Pale flesh to Werner's 1821 nomenclature, the chart later used by field naturalists to describe specimens by eye [1]. The ISCC-NBS computed category for this hex is a pale orange yellow, a soft tan rather than any true skin tone [1]. "Flesh" here follows the old convention of naming a pale tan after light skin; this library keeps that only as a historical name, not a claim about real skin [1]. At this hex our library also records a second name, [[pale-flesh|Flesh Red]], at an identical value, and a close cousin, [[flesh-pink|Flesh Pink]], a touch pinker [1].

The nearest distinct neighbor is [[dusty-peach|Dusty peach]], about 2.9 units away by CIEDE2000, with [[sugar-cane|Sugar Cane]] close behind it [1]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 81, chroma 26, hue 73 degrees, Munsell 7.9YR 8.1/4.2 [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 813 of 23,781 paintings, 3.42 percent, as photographed [2]. It is most over-represented in the 1710s, in 13 of that decade's 169 paintings, about 2.3 times the expected rate [2]. Xugu is its most devoted painter here, carrying it in 9 of his 16 works, over 16 times the baseline, well ahead of Luis de Morales [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment test [2].
